newsitem.title: UK: Lloyd's of London faces two poor years - Names group.
newsitem.headline: Lloyd's of London faces two poor years - Names group.

text.p: Lloyds of London is in a bear market for the insurance industry and investors should think carefully before committing themselves to underwrite in 1997 and 1998, the Association of Lloyd's Members (ALM) said on Tuesday.

"Market conditions this year and next do not look good and investors should be wary of the blandishments of their advisers to write more business," ALM publications editor Robert Miller told a news conference.
Miller was speaking at the launch of the 'Lloyd's Market Results and Prospects' guide by the ALM, the largest independent group for Lloyd's individual backers, known as Names.

"The sorts of return seen in the three golden years 1993, 1994 and 1995 will not be seen in 1996 and 1997. The continued weakness in rates shows few signs of being reversed," the ALM said in a statement

The ALM's pessimistic profit outlook is based on falling premium rates, particularly in the marine insurance market. The fall in rates is part of a cyclical downturn, but commentators are now concerned that some rates appear to be in freefall.
"The 1996 and 1997 underwriting years do not offer particularly appetising prospects for Names and investors," the ALM said.
However, Miller told reporters, "I think conditions will really be very much worse than that."
The ALM's Results and Prospects guide is part of a growth industry in research and analysis in and around Lloyd's following several years of change in the market and the entry of corporate investors.

As well as a market report, the guide includes profiles on all Lloyd's underwriting syndicates, managing agents, members agents, mambers agents pooling arrangements (MAPAs) and quoted Lloyd's investors.

Miller said the ALM guide was unique in analysing managing agents -- the companies which operate syndicates -- which enabled investors to look at agencies and syndicates together as if they were insurance companies.
The guide was compiled in association with Financial Intelligence & Research Limited, which provided most of the accounting data.

Other leading commentators on Lloyds of London are Syndicate Underwriting Research Limited (SURL), Stace Barr Wellington and members agent Christie Brockbank Shipton which acquired Chatset earlier this year.
